name: Nahat
title: Levite in service under King Hezekiah
summary: Nahat was a Levite who served during King Hezekiah's religious reforms in Judah. He was among the Levites appointed to oversee the offerings, tithes, and holy contributions in the house of the Lord. He is also mentioned in the genealogies as a descendant of Levi.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Levi
keyEvents.description: Nahat is mentioned as a descendant of Levi through the line of Kohath in the genealogies of Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's Temple Reform
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah carried out a major religious reform in which he cleansed the temple and restored proper worship. The Levites, including Nahat, played a central role in this work.

keyEvents.title: Oversight of Temple Offerings
keyEvents.description: Nahat was appointed as one of the overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, with responsibility for supervising the offerings, tithes, and holy contributions brought to the house of the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Organization of Temple Service
keyEvents.description: As part of Hezekiah's reforms, the service of the Levites was reorganized to ensure a dignified and orderly worship in the temple in Jerusalem.
